subject.title: feat(exec): verified-human instruction provenance for sensitive targets

question: Should OpenClaw add a gateway-enforced verified-human provenance boundary for sensitive side-effect targets, and should that live in core config, plugin policy APIs, or a staged combination of both?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent boundary changes security semantics, config/API shape, and plugin policy capabilities, which cannot be chosen safely by cleanup automation.

options.title: Design generic core plus plugin seam
options.body: Add the minimal core provenance contract and hook/capability metadata needed for security plugins and core exec/gateway policies to enforce verified-human-sensitive-target rules.

options.title: Stage hook metadata first
options.body: Keep this issue blocked on narrower hook/capability work such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48503 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48510 before defining enforcement.

options.title: Decline new boundary
options.body: Treat existing approvals, sandboxing, allowlists, and separate gateways as the supported model and close the provenance-gating direction after documenting that decision.

recommendation.title: Design generic core plus plugin seam
recommendation.body: Add the minimal core provenance contract and hook/capability metadata needed for security plugins and core exec/gateway policies to enforce verified-human-sensitive-target rules.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent maintainer-review/merge involvement in adjacent agents/runtime work and is one of the issue-timeline subscribers for this security/product surface.
